title: Nététou, Fermented Locust Bean
author: Compiled from CIRAD / ritimo (Ferré & Muchnik; Ndir et al.) and the iru–soumbala literature
desc: Néré (Parkia biglobosa) seeds boiled until soft, dehulled, cooked again, and left three days in a warm room until the mass turns dark, soft, and pungent with ammonia — then salted and sun-dried. The seasoning in ceebu jën, mbakhal and many leaf sauces.
longDesc: Nététou is the Senegalese name for fermented néré (African locust bean) seeds, equivalent to Nigerian iru and Ghanaian dawadawa and, in Burkina Faso, soumbala. The pods are picked April to June, shelled and the pulp removed; the seeds are boiled 12 to 24 hours (15 to 24 ‘until soft’ in the CIRAD market study), the hulls loosened by pounding in a mortar with a little sand, and the cotyledons cooked again (30 minutes in one source, 3 hours in another), drained and cooled. They are left to ferment in a warm room for 48 to 72 hours — 72 in the CIRAD study; Senegalese practice is given as 3 to 4 days in a regional review. The mass is then salted and sun-dried for a day. THE ENDPOINT IS BORROWED: no study measures pH during Senegalese nététou fermentation; the quantified endpoint comes from the same organism and substrate in Nigeria, Burkina Faso and Benin. It is alkaline — the wet mass rises to about pH 7.9 to 8.4 as ammonia is released — and observable: surface growth grows more intense, the seeds soften, darken, and the ammonia smell turns pungent.
ingredients: Néré (Parkia biglobosa) seeds — quantity not printed in any source
Water for boiling, enough to cover
Fine sand, a little, to loosen the hulls in the mortar (optional, as in the ritimo sheet)
Salt — the finished Casamance market product measured 22.6 to 23.2% NaCl; no salting recipe is printed
equipment: Warm, covered fermenting vessel (a ‘fermentation tun’ in the West African studies)
steps: Pods are picked April to June (ritimo sheet); shell them and remove the yellow pulp.
Boil the seeds for 12 to 24 hours (15 to 24 hours ‘until soft’ in the CIRAD market study), topping up with water.
Pound the seeds in a mortar to loosen the hulls; the ritimo sheet says adding sand to the mortar makes the pounding easier. Remove all hulls — dehulling is a safety step (see the warnings).
Cook the cotyledons again: 30 minutes (Ndir et al. 1997) or 3 hours (ritimo sheet) — the two sources disagree. Drain and let cool.
Pile the cooked seeds in a covered vessel in a warm room and leave 48 to 72 hours (72 hours in the CIRAD study; 3 to 4 days in the Senegal regional review).

Judge by the mass, not the clock: surface growth becomes more intense, the seeds are softer, the colour has darkened, the ammonia smell is pungent, and the mass should feel warm (West African studies record it rising from ambient to about 30 to 45 °C). On the WET mass a pH of about 7.9 to 8.4 is the measured endpoint in the iru and soumbala studies.
Salt and sun-dry for at least one day. Pound or shape into balls (balls in Senegal; cones in Mali).
Store dry. Use in small amounts, by the pinch, in the sauce.
chefTips: REJECT CUE: a rotten-egg (hydrogen sulfide) smell means a defective batch — the CIRAD study names H2S production as the most serious spoilage and the cause of unpleasant flavours.
Do the pH check on the wet ferment: it reads about 7.9 at 48 h wet and falls to about 6.1 to 6.6 once dried.
If the mass stays cold and shows no growth, it is not fermenting.
commonMistakes: Eating the beans without the long boil: the Owusu-Kwarteng et al. (2022) review states ‘In general, locust bean is inedible and could be toxic to humans’.
Judging by the clock alone: the sources disagree on 48, 72 and 96 hours.
servedWith: Added in pinches to nokoss (SEN012), mbakhal (SEN037), thiéré mboum (SEN078) and ceebu jën sauces
storage: Dry, in a sealed container, for months; the sources print no storage time.
healthBenefits: Alkaline fermentation raises protein digestibility and thiamine and riboflavin content; a general review of alkaline fermented foods (Owusu-Kwarteng et al. 2022) reports thiamine up about six-fold and riboflavin about three-fold, not measured on nététou specifically.
Very salty — about 23% NaCl in the finished Casamance product.
culturalNote: SAFETY, from the sources: raw locust bean ‘is inedible and could be toxic to humans’ (nitrates, tannins, cyanide, phytates, oxalates), which is why the long boil and dehulling are not optional; lead, cadmium, cobalt and nickel detected in raw seeds were no longer present after dehulling. Nigerian producers sometimes add potassium-carbonate-rich salt; the ritimo sheet records it without comment. This is a documented traditional process, not a verified home protocol; buying nététou is the safer default.
sources: PROCESS (Senegal-specific): Ndir et al. (1997), ‘Caractéristiques microbiologiques et organoleptiques du nététu du commerce’, Cahiers Agricultures 6(4), 299–304 — fragments: ‘beans were boiled for 15-24 h until soft’; ‘cooked for 30 min’; ‘left to ferment for 72 h in a warm room’; ‘salted and sun-dried for 1 day (in Senegal)’. Author string on the fetched page was garbled (‘D’dir … Laurent’), almost certainly Ndir … Lefebvre; verify before citing. Plus the ritimo/dph sheet (‘Nadia Chalabi’ / ‘Nadia CHALABI’, August 1996, crediting Ferré & Muchnik, CIRAD-SAR, L’Harmattan 1995): boil 12–24 h, cook 3 h, ferment 48–72 h; cue ‘forte odeur, goût prononcé, couleur brun foncé’.

ENDPOINT (borrowed, stated): Atere et al. 2020 (iru, Nigeria) — ‘The pH increased significantly from 4.57 in the raw seeds to 8.40 at 96 hr’; sensory progression — surface growth more intense, seeds softer, colour darker, ammonia more pungent; best 48–72 h. Guissou et al. 2020 (soumbala, Burkina Faso): wet pH 6.99 (0 h) to 7.92 (48 h), dried about 6.14. Popoola et al. 2022 (iru): mass warms from ambient to about 30–45 °C; flavour peaks at 48 h, appearance and colour decline by 72 h. Azokpota et al. 2006: afitin 24 h, iru and sonru 48 h, ‘very soft products’.

Senegal-only finished-product data: moisture 38.3–49.1%, NaCl 22.6–23.2% (Casamance); the regional review (Coulibaly Diakite et al. 2020) gives nététu 3–4 days with NO pH, NO temperature and NO completion criterion.

ABSENT, not estimated: seed weights, water volumes, salt amounts. The prep/rest/cook figures take the 15–24 h boil at about 19.5 h plus 30 minutes, and 72 hours of fermentation; the yield is a scheduling estimate.

SAFETY quotes: ‘In general, locust bean is inedible and could be toxic to humans (Wang and Fung, 1996).’ (Owusu-Kwarteng et al. 2022, review of alkaline fermented foods); ‘lead, cadmium, cobalt and nickel were detected in the raw seeds’ and ‘were no longer available after dehulling’ (Atere et al. 2020, iru).
